ExampleMcpServer
public abstract class McpRestServlet extends AbstractMcpRestServlet
Abstract MCP servlet bound to protocol revision 2026-07-28.

Subclass this (rather than the neutral AbstractMcpRestServlet) to expose a 2026-07-28 endpoint at POST /; the revision binding is a compile-time choice made by which class you extend.

URI and polymorphic-type serializer policy (addBeanTypes and uriResolution="NONE") is inherited centrally from the neutral AbstractMcpRestServlet; the only revision-specific behavior added here is notification empty-body processing, below.

Registers McpNotificationResponseProcessor so a null dispatch result (a JSON-RPC notification) renders as a genuinely empty HTTP body instead of the framework's default four-byte null JSON literal.

      createMcpOptions
      

      protected McpOptions createMcpOptions()
      

      Factory method for the behavior configuration published by getMcpOptions().

 
      
 Override to customize any of capabilities/instructions/cache/mrtr/subscriptions/broker in one place. The
 default returns a plain McpOptions (all defaults).

 
      
 Runs eagerly during servlet/RestContext initialization, not lazily on first request:
 getMcpOptions() is itself a @Bean hook, so RestContext's constructor invokes it
 — and therefore this method — while walking the resource's @Bean methods at startup,
 strictly before the embedded server's start() returns. Do not write an override that depends on
 runtime request state or on a port/address only known after start() (e.g. a Jetty ephemeral
 port); that state does not exist yet when this hook runs.

 
      
 Must be side-effect-free and idempotent, exactly like
 AbstractMcpRestServlet.createMcpConfig(): getMcpOptions()
 calls this hook at most once per servlet instance and publishes the result via a lock-free
 AtomicReference.compareAndSet(V, V), so under a first-access race it may be
 invoked by more than one thread, but only one resulting instance is ever published and returned.
      

      

      Returns:
      

      A non-null options instance.

      getMcpOptions
      

      public final McpOptions getMcpOptions()
      

      Returns this servlet's binding-owned McpOptions, built eagerly during initialization.

 
      
 Because this method is annotated @Bean, RestContext's constructor invokes it (and
 therefore createMcpOptions()) while the servlet is initializing — strictly before the
 embedded server's start() returns. This is not deferred to the first incoming HTTP
 request, despite the internal caching below; a createMcpOptions() override must not depend on
 runtime request/port state, since none exists yet at that point. The AtomicReference-backed
 publish below exists only to make repeat/racing invocations of this @Bean method idempotent
 — every call after the first returns the same instance, mirroring exactly how
 getMcpConfig() memoizes
 — not to defer construction itself.
 Also published as a @Bean so downstream plumbing (getSubscriptionBroker(),
 subscriptions/listen dispatch) can resolve it uniformly through the BeanStore. This
 @Bean publication is authoritative and takes precedence over any Spring @Bean McpOptions
 in the app context: a Spring user who wants their configuration honored must inject it INTO
 createMcpOptions()'s override (for example an @Autowired field read from there), not
 publish a bare @Bean McpOptions in their Spring context and expect it to be picked up instead.
      

      

      Returns:
      

      The options. Never null.
      

      Throws:
      

      IllegalStateException - If createMcpOptions() returns null.

      getSubscriptionBroker
      

      public final McpSubscriptionBroker getSubscriptionBroker()
      

      Returns this servlet's lazily-published, binding-owned subscription broker.

 
      
 Reads getMcpOptions()'s memoized McpOptions.getSubscriptionBroker(): an explicitly
 configured broker is returned as-is; otherwise one is derived and memoized per-binding, sized from
 McpOptions.getSubscriptions()'s queue bound (see McpOptions.resolveSubscriptionBroker()).
      

      

      Overrides:
      

      getSubscriptionBroker in class AbstractMcpRestServlet
      

      Returns:
      

      The subscription broker. Never null.

      mcpResourceServerAuth
      

      public final void mcpResourceServerAuth(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest req,
 jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse res)
      

      OAuth 2.1 resource-server bearer gate for the MCP POST / endpoint (READY-312f F2).

 
      
 A no-op unless RS auth is enabled; when enabled, every request the
 router resolves to a POST (the dedicated MCP servlet's only writable surface) must present a valid bearer
 token or it is rejected with 401 / 403 and a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... challenge (see
 McpResourceServerSupport.gateMcpServlet(McpResourceServerConfig, HttpServletRequest, HttpServletResponse)).
 The gate reads the router-resolved method (honoring ?method=/X-Method overrides) rather than
 the raw servlet method, so a method-override cannot slip past it (H3).  The well-known GET routes below are
 intentionally left unauthenticated so a client can discover the PRM document.
      

      

      Parameters:
      

      req - The raw HTTP request.
      

      res - The raw HTTP response (used to emit the challenge header on rejection).

      mcpProtectedResourceMetadataRoot
      

      public McpProtectedResourceMetadata mcpProtectedResourceMetadataRoot(RestRequest req)
      

      Serves the RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata document at the root well-known location (SEP-2351 fallback).

 
      
 This route (and its path-inserted sibling) is registered unconditionally, but returns 404 whenever RS auth
 is disabled — so a non-opted-in servlet claims the well-known
 namespace but exposes no observable metadata (READY-312f F2, M7).
      

      

      Parameters:
      

      req - The REST request.
      

      Returns:
      

      The PRM document.
